In the old days requiring a CD check didn't seem so bad. Sometimes the disc was required to get music in the game but only because it was uncompressed audio. I think Age of Empires and Star Wars X-wing vs. Tie Fighter were like this. Even before then sometimes you had to look in the manual to answer a challenge-response block. These all seemed fine while you still had the physical items.

Eventually the DRM became so invasive it would refuse to start if it even thought certain software was present on your and the worst versions could gimp your computer with security bugs, like the worst version of SecuROM. These days there are reports of Denuvo or other DRM running thousands of times per second reducing performance.

Then there is the issue of always-online DRM. You can't do shit if your internet connection goes down, the company's internet connection goes down, or they decide to pull the plug on their servers. People lost music libraries when Microsoft and everyone else decided to terminate their PlaysForSure services meaning the things they had "bought" could no longer be used.
